context:
Goal: your Mac coordinator starts its lane sessions with no click from you.
Problem (goal): the desktop app starts a session with no card only on a turn you typed. On any other turn it refuses the start even after you press allow, and no setting changes that.
Based on (measured): Mac probes 2026-11-06, Claude 2.1.296: user_asked on your typed turn, no card, 3 of 3; offer, a card; user_asked on a wake turn, a card, then refused after allow; a Remote Control turn, refused.
Based on (ruling): your note on this item, 14:01 CST: 'how can these be your answers' after A and B started with no work. Probe 3 since showed the no-card start needs a turn you typed, so this asks again.
Based on (doc): "Allow rules have no effect in bypassPermissions" (code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md).
Departs from: decision lanes-start-as-agents on main, "each Mac lane start is one press" — becomes the pick below.
Meanwhile: PR #1339 (probe results) waits with the batch runner; the lane builds your pick when it lands.
holds: How the Mac coordinator starts lane sessions.

lastAnswer.note: are we still waiting on the probe

options.gain: No cards; one line from you starts a whole batch; keeps your 11-04 ruling that a lane is a session (item 168).
options.how: The coordinator queues ready lanes. When you type to it in the desktop app ("start the lanes", or any message), it starts every queued lane on that turn.
options.label: One typed line per batch
options.lose: A lane that becomes ready while you are away waits for your next typed line. Typing from your phone over Remote Control does not start them.

options.gain: No line and no card, ever, even while you are away.
options.how: Mac lanes run as background agents inside the coordinator, not as sessions.
options.label: Lanes as background agents
options.lose: Goes against your 11-04 ruling (item 168, a lane is a session). A lane ends when the coordinator's session ends, and lanes share its machine.

options.label: Keep a card per lane start
options.lose: On a turn you did not type, the card no longer works (probe 3 was refused after allow), so lanes wait for you anyway.

reply: Yes, still waiting. Probe 4 (item 300) was refused at its step 2 by our own hand-made-worktree guard, so the claude -p start was never measured. The lane rewrites the probe with EnterWorktree. This question comes back with real options once that result is in.
title: How should your Mac coordinator start lanes with no click?
why: Your ask (13:24 CST): local coordinators still need your press to start each lane.
